# What I made of my friend's page

## 1. My answer

**What I'd do:** I'd open an account at **פסגות ניירות ערך** (Psagot) and buy **"ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)", fund number 5139282**. That means putting in 10,000 ₪ now and 500 ₪ a month for 10 years.

**How much I'd end up with:** The page says **86,492 ₪**, after I've put in **70,000 ₪** of my own. It says that's "בכסף של היום, אחרי דמי ניהול ומס" (in today's money, after fees and tax), "אם הדולר לא זז מול השקל" (if the dollar doesn't move against the shekel). That figure assumes 7% a year, and the page itself says 7% is "תשואה לדוגמה, לא תחזית" (an example return, not a forecast). So 86,492 is an illustration, not a promise.

**How sure I am:** Fairly sure about the account, less sure about the fund.

- **The account:** Psagot comes out well ahead. The page says it costs me **1,057 ₪** over 10 years. The next one, לאומי (Leumi), costs **4,541 ₪**, and some cost over 20,000 ₪. That's a clear gap I can understand.
- **The fund:** It wins by very little. The runner-up, **אלטשולר שחם מחקה, 5139100**, is only "‎−43 ₪" behind. Both funds also say "שנה אחת" (one year), which I take to mean they only have one year of history. That bothers me for money I'm leaving alone for 10 years. The next ones, KTF and הראל (Harel), have 4 years of history and cost about 447 ₪ less over the 10 years. I might pay that to buy something with a longer record.
- **Before I do anything:** I'd phone Psagot and ask whether I really get their standing-order price. The page says only "3 מתוך 15" (3 out of 15) firms publish a cheaper price for monthly standing orders.

So what does it mean for my money? Roughly 86,000 ₪ in today's money, if the market does what the page assumes. The difference between the best choice and the worst one on the list is more than 20,000 ₪, which is the part I really took away.

## 2. The parts I actually used

- The top: the headline "איפה ואיך הכי זול להשקיע במדד, לאורך זמן" (where and how to invest in an index most cheaply, over time), the S&P 500 button and the four boxes I could fill in (סכום היום, הפקדה חודשית, שנים, תשואה בשנה: amount today, monthly deposit, years, yearly return).
- The big result box: "הפקדתם 70,000 ₪" (you deposited) next to "הבחירה שלכם · ★ הזול" (your choice, the cheapest) at **86,492 ₪**.
- The list on the right, "כל החשבונות" (all the accounts), showing what each bank leaves me and what it charges.
- The list on the left, "כל הקרנות על מדד S&P 500" (all the S&P 500 funds), mostly the top few rows.
- The fund card showing "דמי ניהול: 0% קבועים 0% משתנים" (management fees: 0% fixed, 0% variable).
- The table under "מה הכי משנה את מה שיישאר לכם" (what changes your result the most).

## 3. Going down the page, block by block

1. **Top menu (מקור, מדריך, חברות ומסלולים…):** Skipped it. I was already on the right tab.
2. **Headline and subtitle:** Read it. "בוחרים חשבון ניירות ערך וקרן, ורואים כמה יישאר לכם" (choose an account and a fund, and see what you'll keep) is exactly my question. Good start.
3. **Index buttons and the S&P 500 description:** Read it. "האתר לא ממליץ על מדד" (the site doesn't recommend an index) was fine with me, since I'd already chosen. "אפשר להחזיק אותו גם דרך קרן חוץ" (you can also hold it through a foreign fund) puzzled me a little.
4. **The four sliders:** Used them. They already matched my plan, apart from the 7%, which I can't judge.
5. **The "אינפלציה" (inflation) button and the line next to it:** Confused me. It mentions the dollar at 3.17 ₪ and "הבנק המרכזי האירופי" (the European Central Bank). Why Europe, when I'm investing in America from Israel?
6. **The result box:** Used it heavily. One line, "(הערה לבדוק: הסכום מעוגל לשקל, לפי מסמך השיטה)" ("note to check: the amount is rounded to the shekel, according to the method document"), looked like a note someone left for themselves. It made me wonder whether the number was final.
7. **"כמה זה עולה לכם ב־10 שנים, בכל אחד מהזוגות" (what it costs you in 10 years, for each pair) and the coloured bar:** Skimmed it. I only took in the three numbers underneath. The account costs "1 ₪ יותר" (1 ₪ more) than the next-best pair, the fund "58 ₪ פחות" (58 ₪ less) and tax "14 ₪ יותר" (14 ₪ more). Paying more tax because I make more profit is fine. But these amounts are tiny, so the top two choices are really the same.
8. **The Psagot account card:** Used it: "מה החשבון גובה ב־10 שנים: 1,057 ₪" (what the account charges over 10 years). I noted "קיבלתם מחיר אחר? הזינו אותו" (got a different price? enter it) in case my bank offers me a deal.
9. **The fund card:** Used it, but there's jargon: "נאמן 0.02%" (trustee, 0.02%), "קרן מחקה" (tracking fund), "4D".
10. **The filter buttons ("עסקת החלף", "חשיפה לדולר", "צוברת" and others):** Skipped them. I don't know what most of them mean (some are explained in section 5).
11. **The fund list:** Read the top 4–5 rows, then skimmed. The foreign funds all say "אין מחיר כאן" (no price here), so I gave up on them.
12. **The single currency-hedged fund (הראל, 5127527):** Read it and got scared off. It shows "‎−2.44%" against the index, and a range "בין +2,212 ₪ ל־‎−23,766 ₪" (between +2,212 ₪ and −23,766 ₪).
13. **"למה חלק מהקרנות בלי מחיר בפסגות" (why some funds have no price at Psagot):** Skimmed it. The line about what "מול המדד" (against the index) means was useful, but it took two readings.
14. **The accounts list on the right:** Used it fully (see section 4).
15. **"מה הכי משנה את מה שיישאר לכם" (what changes your result the most) and its chart:** Used the table, skimmed the chart. The lesson: "הכי ישנה מספר השנים" (the number of years changes it most). Two extra years adds **19,116 ₪**, and 600 ₪ a month instead of 500 adds **14,474 ₪**. That's practical advice I can act on.
16. **"עם נטרול מט"ח או בלי: מה קרה בפועל" (with or without currency hedging: what actually happened), plus its three cards, two charts and table:** Mostly confused me. It's long and heavy. In the end I read "השורה התחתונה" (the bottom line): hedging "לא מגן מירידה של השוק" (doesn't protect against a market fall). I also read that over those 4 years the unhedged fund would have left "9,460 ₪ יותר" (9,460 ₪ more). That was enough for me to stay unhedged.
17. **"מתחילים מבחירה אחת, ורואים מה משפר אותה ובכמה" (start from one choice and see what improves it, and by how much), the staircase chart:** Confused me. It starts from "עכשיו: MTF סל S&P 500 (4D), ירושלים" (now: an MTF fund at Bank of Jerusalem) at 79,176 ₪. I never chose that, and I don't know why the page thinks it's what I have now. The steps up (+4,972 ₪ for a different account, +2,344 ₪ for a different fund) did show me why Psagot plus Ylin wins.
18. **The small table under the staircase:** Skimmed it. The minus signs and plus signs in "עלות החשבון ‎−5,416" (account cost) and "מס +444" (tax) confused me. Is minus good or bad here?
19. **"חשבון אחר, אותה קרן" (a different account, same fund) / "סוג קרן אחר, אותו חשבון" (a different type of fund, same account):** Skimmed them. The useful line was that buying the fund abroad, "קרן שנקנית בחו"ל", leaves me **20,100 ₪ less**. Decision made: no foreign fund.
20. **Notes at the bottom:** Read them, and one worried me: "בתשואה של 0% או של 10% הסדר משתנה ב־6 מקומות" (at a 0% or 10% return, the order changes in 6 places). So is Psagot still first if the market does badly? It doesn't say directly.
21. **Footer:** Read it. "אישי, לא מסחרי, בלי קישורי שיווק" (personal, non-commercial, no marketing links) and "נתונים נכון ל־05.11.2026" (data as of 05.11.2026). Both made me trust it more.

## 4. Lists, tables and charts: what I looked at

- **Accounts list (right):** I looked at the bank name, the big "נשאר" number (what's left for me) and the small number under it, which I took to be the cost. I read the grey "לא בחישוב" (not in the calculation) lines to see whether I qualify for a special price. They're for "צעירים, חיילים משוחררים, סטודנטים" (young people, discharged soldiers, students), so not for me. I ignored the coloured bars. The legend (orange "עמלות קנייה ומכירה" for buy/sell fees, yellow "דמי משמרת" for custody fees, red "דמי ניהול חשבון" for account fees, pink "המרת מטבע" for currency conversion, grey "העמלות זו על זו" for fees on fees) was too much to match up with the bars. Rows 3 and 10 were cut off in the screenshots, so I don't know which banks they are.
- **Funds list (left):** I looked at the fund name and the right-hand column, "לעומת הבחירה" (compared with the choice). That's the shekel figure I understand. I glanced at the "מול המדד" (against the index) column, mainly to notice "שנה אחת" (one year) against "4 שנים" (4 years). I ignored all the coloured tags and the fund numbers, except to write down 5139282.
- **"מה הכי משנה" chart:** I ignored the lines and the "50% פחות … 50% יותר" (50% less … 50% more) axis and used the table below it. The columns I used were "בתוכנית שלכם" (your plan), "אחרי השינוי" (after the change) and "ההפרש" (the difference).
- **Dollar bar chart, fund bar chart and the hedging table:** I looked at the white "‎+13.4 / ‎−12.5" bars and at 2022, where everything went down. In the table I only read the last row, "4 השנים יחד" (the 4 years together): hedged **+35.9%** against unhedged **+50.4% to +56.8%**. I ignored the column "עם נטרול מול בלי נטרול, בנקודות אחוז" (hedged versus unhedged, in percentage points).
- **The staircase:** I read the three numbers at the top (79,176 → +4,972 → +2,344) and "הכי הרבה 86,492 ₪" (the most: 86,492 ₪). I ignored the colour key and the wavy line at the bottom of the grey bar.

## 5. What I didn't understand

- **"בכסף של היום" (in today's money).** Does it mean the bank will actually show about 86,000 ₪, or more, with inflation already taken off? This matters a lot to me.
- **Is 7% before or after inflation?**
- **"4D" and "4A".**
- **"קרן מחקה" against "קרן סל".** Both seem to be tracking funds of some kind, but I don't know how they differ.
- **"עסקת החלף" (I think, a swap), "צוברת" (I think, a fund that reinvests the dividends), "נאמן" (trustee).**
- **"דמי משמרת" (custody fees).**
- **"W-8BEN", "UCITS", and "מס עיזבון אמריקאי".** That last one is American estate tax. That sounds frightening at my age, and nothing explains it.
- **"כל עוד יש רווח ריאלי, 25% מכל הפרש בין הקרנות הולך למס"** ("as long as there's a real profit, 25% of every difference between the funds goes to tax").
- **Why the staircase starts at Bank of Jerusalem with an MTF fund.**
- **Why the dollar rate comes from the European Central Bank.**

## 6. What I wanted to know and couldn't find

- **How much in actual shekels**, not "today's money".
- **What if the market falls in the years just before I need the money?** I'm 61 and will be 71 at the end. Can I take money out partway through, and what does that cost?
- **Is Psagot safe and reliable?** What happens to my money if the company has problems?
- **How do I actually open the account and set up the monthly purchase?** Is it on the phone, at a branch, or online only?
- **My own bank's price.** I'd have to type it in myself.
- **Which 6 places change when the return is 0% or 10%**, and whether Psagot stays first. There's a "פירוט" (details) link, but no details on the page itself.
- **Whether a one-year-old fund is a risk.**

## 7. If half the page had to go

First to go would be the whole hedging section, "עם נטרול מט"ח או בלי" (charts, cards, table and sources). It's the longest part, and all I needed from it was one sentence: unhedged has done better and hedging doesn't protect against a crash.

Next, the filter buttons and all the coloured tags on the funds, and the coloured cost bars with their legend. After that, the staircase and the small table under it, which repeat the lists in a more confusing way. Then the foreign funds that have "אין מחיר כאן" (no price here).

I'd keep the sliders, the result box, the accounts list, the top of the funds list, and the "מה הכי משנה" (what changes it most) table.
